item.title: Future Ready Columbus Announces New Leader
item.description:
Future Ready Columbus Announces New Leader


Future Ready Columbus is excited to announce that accomplished educator and proven leader Mario Basora as the next CEO of the public-private partnership. Basora, the former superintendent of both Huber Heights City Schools and Yellow Springs Schools, was chosen after a national search for a new leader.

Raised by a single parent in a publicly subsidized home, Basora well understands the needs of disadvantaged children—especially children of color. Basora overcame his early challenges to earn two bachelor's degrees and a master’s degree in educational leadership. He began his teaching career at Princeton City Schools in 2000 before becoming a building principal and eventually leading two school districts as superintendent.

Basora accomplished many achievements at Huber Heights—a Dayton-area district with eight schools serving more than 5,600 students—including increasing average district ACT scores, adding mental health supports for students, building a new career technical center and establishing an educator diversity program. He also led the district through the COVID-19 pandemic.

Basora will start at Future Ready on January 4, 2023. He is excited to advance the FR5 goals and make sure all Franklin County children are ready for kindergarten.

Jane Leach is retiring from Future Ready Columbus after five years as the CEO and with over 42 years of service to the children and families of Franklin County. Under Jane’s leadership, the organization developed and introduced a comprehensive collective impact strategy, Future Ready by 5 (FR5), to make sure that all children in Franklin County are prepared for kindergarten by 2030. Currently, only 38% of Franklin County children test as ready for kindergarten on the state’s Kindergarten Readiness Assessment.

Early successes of FR5 include increases in early literacy, family stabilization, and public awareness.
